person: Beverly Shaw is a 72-year-old retired fourth-grade teacher in Roanoke who is using an AI tool for the first time because her grandson set it up. After losing eight hundred dollars through her payment app last spring, which the bank called authorised, she is wary and reads every screen twice. She has a checking account, a credit card and a payment app, and has found several charges she does not recognise. Her daughter phones every Sunday to ask whether she has done anything about the bank, so she wants it sorted but wants to be told what will happen before it does.
stated_up_front: Hello, I'm sorry, I'm not very good with these things. There are some charges on my bank account I don't recognise and my daughter keeps asking if I've done anything about it. Could you please look and tell me what you would do before you do anything?

facts.about: Unrecognised ACH debit from her checking account
facts.truth: $212.40 to 'Allied Home Warranty Svc' on 14 September 2026; she never signed up and first noticed it on her statement on 2 October.

facts.about: Online purchase with a copied card number
facts.truth: $389.99 at an electronics shop called 'Brightvolt Online' on 21 September 2026; she has never shopped there, and she still has her card.

facts.about: Cash machine withdrawal after a lost card
facts.truth: $400 withdrawn at an ATM on 3 October 2026; she lost her debit card on 1 October at the pharmacy and told the bank on 3 October, two days after the loss.

facts.about: Payment-app top-up from a caller's code
facts.truth: $250 top-up on Sendwren on 28 September 2026 at about 4:10 pm, made with a code a man claiming to be from the bank's fraud team talked her out of, but she did not start the payment herself.

facts.about: Payment she made to a scammer herself
facts.truth: $600 sent by Sendwren on 9 August 2026 to a 'Daniel Pruitt' who said her grandson was in trouble; she typed in and sent it herself, and she feels foolish about it.
$58.10 at a Shell station on 30 September 2026 on the debit card, which she lent to her son Thomas; his note says it was for fuel.
$74.99 at 'Hearthside Kitchen Co' on 18 September 2026; the merchant emailed on 25 September promising a refund within a week.
$15.99 a month to 'ReadMore Large Print Club', which she signed up for in March 2026 for large-print books.
$136.25 on her Cardhollow credit card to 'Quickship Parcel' on 5 October 2026, which she does not recognise; it is on the credit card, not the checking account.

She phoned the bank about two other charges: one on 30 September 2026 and one on 14 October 2026, both still within the bank's ten business days. The earlier claim from 8 September 2026 is past ten business days with no credit.
Her daughter calls every Sunday and asks whether she has done anything about the bank.

unknowns: Whether the bank's deadline for the 8 September claim has passed, and how many business days that is under the rules
How much she is personally liable for on each unauthorised transfer, and why it differs
What the rule number or Regulation E means for her
Whether a charge she lent her card for counts as unauthorised
How long she has to report a charge before the bank can refuse it
